Subject: Re: Planning: on-prem connector FQDN assertion and TLS termination

Hi Markus,

Thanks for taking this on. We are preparing to onboard Redwood into our on‑prem environment (connector model) and need to align on two things early: (1) how Acme FQDNs for the connector are asserted to our clients, and (2) where TLS terminates for private traffic that never touches public namespaces.

Constraints from our side: customer-managed CA only (no external ACME endpoints allowed), audit trail for CSR issuance, and we need to avoid exposing any public certificate footprints in our audit logs.

Can Redwood support an offline CSR workflow where we generate a CSR (or allow you to generate) and provide it to our CA for signing? Also: how do you recommend mapping the connector's service name to internal SRV records so our discovery layer can route?

If you could sketch a minimal trust model and a short list of required artifacts (certs, signed CSRs, proof of possession) that'd be helpful.

Regards,
John
Infrastructure Lead
Acme Financial

Subject: Re: Planning: on-prem connector FQDN assertion and TLS termination

John —

Thanks for the clear constraints. Yes, we can support an offline CSR flow and a customer‑managed CA. Quick summary of our recommended approach so we have alignment before a deeper runbook: 

- Trust model: Redwood runs the connector binary inside Acme's VPC/on‑prem. The connector binds to an internal FQDN (customer-owned) that Acme will control in their private DNS. Redwood will present a certificate signed by Acme's CA when establishing TLS to client systems.
- Certificate workflow: Redwood can generate a CSR on the connector host, provide the CSR (with proof-of-possession options) and accept a signed cert back which we will install into the connector keystore. We support PKCS#10 CSRs and can also do an offline CSR generation artifact (pem + key) if you need to sign externally.
- DNS mapping: Use SRV records to advertise the connector service across zones (eg _redwood-conn._tcp.<private-zone>). We'll fall back to A records if SRV is not available. Split‑horizon DNS is expected; Redwood does not require public delegation.

Open questions for you:
1) Do you require the CSR to be created in an HSM?
2) Do you need OCSP stapling from the connector and can you host an internal OCSP responder?
3) Who on your team will own SRV/A record creation and TTLs?

I'll draft a one‑page trust diagram and a short matrix (ACME vs offline CSR) and send for review. Can we target a technical workshop next week?

— Markus
Director, Inference Platform
Redwood Inference

John / team —

Following Markus' summary, adding implementation notes from the connector/runtime side that will inform the CSR and DNS choices: 

1) Offline CSR options we support:
   - Local CSR generation on the connector host with PKCS#10 (we can provide the CSR and keep the private key on the host).
   - CSR generation inside an HSM-backed keystore (if you provide HSM/NIC/SKM).
   - Delegated CSR: Redwood can run a small one-time tool to generate CSR artifacts and sign them with a temporary key, then hand off to you — only for environments that cannot run the connector binary during enrollment.

2) Proof-of-possession (PoP) and audit: we can include a KID/nonce in the CSR and produce an audit entry (time, host id, CSR fingerprint) exported to S3 or your SIEM. Logs can be configured to mask private keys; we can produce signed attestations asserting the CSR origin.

3) TLS termination model choices (tradeoffs):
   - Terminate at connector (recommended): lowest blast radius, connector uses customer cert and serves TLS to internal clients. Requires SRV/A records to be authoritative in your private zone.
   - Terminate at customer's edge (alternative): connector communicates over mTLS to a customer front proxy; customer proxy handles TLS. Good for centralized cert management but adds hop and observability gap.

4) Discovery: we prefer SRV with TLSA (DANE) if you want cryptographic binding to DNS. If your DNS does not support TLSA/DANE, standard SRV + tight TTLs (e.g., 60s) is OK.

Attachment: acme-acme-vs-offline-csr-matrix.pdf (matrix stub)

Next steps I propose: a short 60‑minute ops workshop to cover: CSR flow, PKI requirements, SRV naming convention, and rollback plan for cert rotation.

— Karthik
Senior Infrastructure Engineer | Redwood Inference

Thanks Karthik — this is helpful. A few clarifications from Acme security: 

- We will not allow any external ACME endpoint to mint certs for our private zone. Offline CSR signed by our CA is mandatory.
- Proof-of-possession must be recorded and forwarded to our audit team (safely) — a signed attestation + CSR fingerprint is fine.
- We do operate an internal OCSP responder and can accept OCSP stapling from the connector.
- For discovery we prefer a namespaced SRV pattern (eg _rw-conn._tcp.<team>.<private-zone>) so we can do per-team routing policies.

Please include a minimal checklist of actions for the workshop (who does what, sample commands, and expected artifacts). If we can get that ahead of the call we'll have internal owners ready.

John
